raw_response:
I'm 65 now, been farming these fields in Quzhou for 50 years. Just me and my old lady at home — our children work in Shijiazhuang and only come back for Spring Festival. We have 10 mu of land, not big but it's what we have. We do wheat in winter and maize in summer, same as everyone around here.

My wheat went in last October, around the 10th. I bought improved seed from the cooperative, about 35 yuan per mu. Before planting I spread one bag of compound fertilizer on each mu and rotary tilled it in. That part is done. Now it's April and the wheat is at jointing — this is when you have to pay attention. I'll topdress with urea soon, about 20 jin per mu. My neighbor Old Zhang tried saving money last year and only used 12 jin, but his wheat turned yellow and the ears were small. I'd rather spend a bit more than lose the yield — we need that wheat for flour and to sell some. I'll also irrigate twice more: once now at jointing, and again when the wheat is heading in May. The pump uses electricity and that costs money, but without water the yield drops badly. I'll spray herbicide once more, and if the weather turns warm and wet I'll spray fungicide too — can't let rust ruin it.

For the summer maize, as soon as the wheat comes off in early June — maybe the 8th or 10th — I have to plant fast. That window is only about a week. I hire the combine for wheat harvest because we're too old to cut it by hand now, and then I get the tractor in to plant the maize. I always buy hybrid seed, don't save it. Costs about 50-something yuan per mu. At planting I put one bag of compound fertilizer per mu in the row. When the maize is at the big trumpet stage — knee-high or so — I'll topdress with about 25 jin of urea per mu if the leaves look yellow. If it rains well I might skip it, but usually I need it. I'll irrigate twice: once when it's tasseling, that's the critical time, and once when the grain is filling in late August. One spray of herbicide for the maize should be enough.

Labor is tight with just us two old people. During wheat harvest and maize planting I'll hire 2-3 workers for several days — maybe 4 days for wheat and 6 days for maize. We pay them 100 yuan a day. We can't manage the heavy work alone anymore.

Money is always a worry. Seed, fertilizer, diesel for the pump, chemicals, hired help — it all adds up. I reckon I'll spend around 6,500 yuan on everything this year. The wheat should give me about 410 kg per mu, and the maize about 460 kg per mu if the weather holds and we don't get a bad drought. That's enough to eat, sell a bit, and get by. We don't get rich, but we've managed 50 years this way.
